One assessable differential assay routine combines controlled performance, observation and explanation of why reducing-carbohydrate and enzymatic glucose assays answer different questions. Molecular structure and enzyme action are the explanations necessary for this single comparison. The new wording makes that common explanatory product explicit.

A reducing-test-only procedure without the enzymatic distinction is incomplete for this target; an enzyme-specificity statement without controlled assay evaluation/performance is also incomplete. The components can be practiced in stages while remaining one coherent comparative competence. No unrelated standalone enzyme topic or requirement to perform every named classical method is added.

The perform operator remains a real acquisition obligation. Design plausibility is not practical success or actual learner mastery.

One structure/property competence: classify amino-acid side chains and explain the bounded behavior of those same free amino acids. Classification supplies the structural distinctions used by the explanation; pH-dependent charge is a condition of that explanation.

The missing case-2 observations affect P completeness, not semantic minimality. Retain the classification core and independent A verdict while fixing only the material.

One systematic naming procedure for simple2-amino carboxylic acids. Numbering, identifying substituent position and mapping between name and connectivity are components and checks of the same procedure.

The e9d prerequisite supplies a narrower amino-acid foundation; neither Fischer/R/S assignment nor a separate experiment is imported into the naming goal.

One causal explanatory product distinguishes an enzyme-limited digestion step from a transport-limited intestinal uptake step. Changing the English term to intestinal absorption names the same process; it introduces no second output or diagnostic investigation.

Hydrolysis and uptake are distinct mechanisms whose contrast is essential to explaining individual differences. Knowing just one mechanism or reciting the two labels does not complete that comparison. Existing enzyme and digestive-juice goals remain prerequisite context.

No genetic testing, clinical diagnosis or real practical operator is newly introduced.
